title: Grateful Dead Live at Shrine Exposition Hall on 1967-11-10
source: Source: 8 Track Master Reel > 1st Gen Reel (7.5ips) > PCM (Sony Beta ESXHiFi/L-750) - Given to Tim Dalton by Bob Menke; Transfer: PCM > Sony SL-10 > Sony PCM-601ESD > Behringer Ultramatch Pro > Tascam DA-3000 > WAV 16/44.1 - Transferred By Charlie Miller; Lineage: wav > Adobe Audition 1.5 > iZotope RX6 Advanced > iZotope 5 Advanced > CD Wave > TLH > Flac 16; edited and mastered SIRMick February 2018

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear soundboard capture of a blazing 1967 show highlighted by a monster 15‑minute “Viola Lee Blues” and incendiary renditions of “Morning Dew”, “Alligator”, “Caution” and the Cryptical/Too/Cryptical suite.
ai_review.review: The recording is an excellent multi‑track soundboard source that delivers pristine clarity, letting every instrument shine. The performance is a high‑energy showcase from late ’67, with standout moments on Viola Lee Blues, Morning Dew, Alligator, Caution and the Cryptical > Too > Cryptical sequence, while the band’s interplay feels tight and exhilarating throughout.

ai_rating.rationale: Overwhelmingly positive reviews (many 5‑star) praise both the show’s musical firepower and the recording’s superb clarity, indicating an exceptional concert capture.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Multiple reviewers call the sound “great”, “amazing sounding”, and note the multi‑track source provides clear instrument separation; no significant drop‑outs or muffiness mentioned.

standout_songs: Caution (Do Not Step on the Tracks)
show_quality.setlist_flow: The set flows through a powerful opening with Viola Lee Blues, moves into concise early‑era numbers and builds to an intense second half featuring the Cryptical/Too suite and a soaring Caution, maintaining momentum throughout.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for rapid‑fire solos, memorable riffs, and overall strong guitar work; one reviewer notes his fretwork is repetitive but still effective in the era context.
band_member_comments.Phil: Described as more aggressive than earlier ’67 performances, providing a solid bass foundation that drives the high‑energy moments.
band_member_comments.Bob: Highlighted for organ work and distinctive vocal/half‑rap style on Schoolgirl and Alligator; his presence is noted as holding its own throughout.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s organ (and possible early synth textures) receive positive mention, especially during New Potato Caboose and the cryptic sections.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey Hart’s congas add extra fire to Alligator; overall drum work supports the tight, high‑energy groove.
